newsitem.title: CHINA: China rules out Shenzhen, Hong Kong bourse merger.
newsitem.headline: China rules out Shenzhen, Hong Kong bourse merger.

text.p: China's top securities regulator on Thursday quashed rumours that Shenzhen's stock market might be merged with the Hong Kong bourse after the British colony returns to Chinese rule next year.
"The Shenzhen exchange absolutely will not be merged into the Hong Kong bourse after 1997," said Zhou Daojiong, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC).
However, the two exchanges would cooperate after the transfer of power in Hong Kong, he said.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.

Securities-industry officials in Shenzhen, which borders on Hong Kong, have voiced concern over the Shenzhen exchange's viability once the much larger bourse across the border comes under China's control.
Shenzhen exchange officials have said they wanted more cooperation with Hong Kong and have suggested trading and information links.
Zhou also told reporters the CSRC would not interfere in regulatory matters in Hong Kong after 1997 and would not set up an office in the territory.
